title: A fractional dive

blocks.text: A substation-upgrade model has binaries $`x_j`$, and an LP solver you can call with some of them fixed. Write the dive that turns LP points into a plan.

Write `dive(lp)` in `dive.py`. `lp` is a function: `lp(fixed)` takes a dict from variable to 0 or 1 and returns the LP optimum with those variables fixed, as a dict from every variable to its value, or `None` when that LP has no solution. Repeat:

items: Call `lp(fixed)`, starting with `fixed = {}`. If the point has no fractional variable (every value within $`10^{-6}`$ of 0 or 1), return `(plan, steps)`: `plan` maps each variable to its value rounded to 0 or 1.
Otherwise pick the fractional variable with the smallest $`\min(x_j, 1 - x_j)`$ (ties by name), and set `target` to 1 if $`x_j \ge 0.5`$, else 0.

Call `lp` with `fixed` plus $`x_j`$ = `target`. If that returns `None`, use the other value instead. Add the fixing to `fixed`, record `(variable, value)` in `steps`, and go back to step 1 with the point you got.

blocks.text: If both values of a variable give `None`, return `(None, steps)`. A failed fixing is not a step: `steps` holds only the fixings that were kept, so the variable whose two values both failed is not in it. The reference solution appends to `steps` only after a call returns a point. The tests give you an `lp` that answers only the calls a correct dive makes.

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Callable

EPS = 1e-6
LP = Callable[[dict[str, int]], "dict[str, float] | None"]


def dive(lp: LP) -> tuple[dict[str, int] | None, list[tuple[str, int]]]:
    """Fix the least fractional variable to its nearest value, re-solve, repeat until the point is 0-1."""
    fixed: dict[str, int] = {}
    steps: list[tuple[str, int]] = []
    x = lp(fixed)
    while True:
        fractional = [j for j, v in x.items() if EPS < v < 1 - EPS]
        if not fractional:
            return {j: round(v) for j, v in x.items()}, steps
        j = min(fractional, key=lambda j: (min(x[j], 1 - x[j]), j))
        target = 1 if x[j] >= 0.5 else 0
        new = lp({**fixed, j: target})
        if new is None:
            target = 1 - target
            new = lp({**fixed, j: target})
            if new is None:
                return None, steps
        fixed[j] = target
        steps.append((j, target))
        x = new


if __name__ == "__main__":
    answers = {(): {"a": 1, "b": 0.9, "c": 0.4}, (("b", 1),): {"a": 1, "b": 1, "c": 0}}
    print(dive(lambda fixed: answers[tuple(sorted(fixed.items()))]))

print("dive over s1, s2, s3:", dive(lp))

cases.says: of 0.9 and 0.4, the variable at 0.9 is fixed first, at 1, and the next LP point is a plan
of 0.1 and 0.6, the variable at 0.1 is fixed first, at 0
when fixing at the nearest value makes the LP infeasible, the variable is fixed the other way
the second LP is asked with both fixings, not only the newest one
when both values of a variable fail, the dive gives up and its steps leave that variable out
